rows.rationale: Git documents revision selection and --verify object-name resolution. Lane policy accepts a commit object only after object identity and landed/pushed ancestry are established.
rows.proposition: Commit object IDs may select commits; acceptance additionally requires landed and pushed ancestry.

rows.rationale: A tree is not a commit object. Commit-ish peeling does not convert a direct tree identity into an acceptable commit; lane policy refuses it as an invalid revision.
rows.proposition: Tree object IDs are not commits and are refused.

rows.rationale: A blob is not a commit object. Lane policy requires unique object identity that resolves to a commit before ancestry checks.
rows.proposition: Blob object IDs are not commits and are refused.

rows.rationale: Git's commit-ish peeling permits a uniquely selected tag object that resolves to a commit. Lane policy still requires the exact tag object identity and the peeled commit's landed/pushed ancestry.
rows.proposition: Annotated tag object IDs peeling to commits are commit-ish; acceptance additionally requires landed and pushed ancestry.

rows.rationale: Commit-ish peeling only accepts a tag whose target resolves to a commit; a tag peeling to a tree, blob, or other non-commit remains an invalid revision under lane policy.
rows.proposition: Annotated tag object IDs peeling to non-commits are refused.
